title: Requests for Chamber debates on International Men’s Day and AI safety
label: 20 October 2026 · Backbench Debates
summary: The Backbench Business Committee heard two applications for debates: Peter Swallow asked for a Chamber debate on International Men’s Day (19 Nov) about men’s health, education, family roles and paternity leave; Iqbal Mohamed asked for a Chamber debate on the safety of ‘frontier’ AI and urged fast parliamentary action, proposing pharma-style regulation for AI. Both speakers said they would accept Westminster Hall if the Chamber wasn’t available. The Committee raised scheduling and departmental-responsibility issues and will decide in private.

chapters.title: Committee introduces two debate requests
chapters.takeaway: Two MPs asked for Chamber debates; both preferred the main Chamber but would accept Westminster Hall if needed.

turns.speaker: Chair
turns.text: We will hear two applications for debates in the Chamber or Westminster Hall. First up: Peter Swallow on International Men’s Day.

chapters.title: International Men’s Day: what Peter Swallow asked for
chapters.takeaway: Mr Swallow asked for a Chamber debate on 19 November to highlight men's health, education gaps, family roles and paternity leave, but accepted Westminster Hall if necessary.

turns.speaker: Peter Swallow
turns.text: On 19 November the UK joins over 80 countries for International Men’s Day. I want a Commons debate to continue the useful tradition of focusing on issues affecting men and boys.

turns.speaker: Peter Swallow
turns.text: Key concerns are implementing the men’s health strategy, the mental health crisis among young men and boys, and educational gaps—especially for white working-class boys.

turns.speaker: Peter Swallow
turns.text: There are positives to discuss too: day one paternity leave started in April, and the Government is reviewing parental leave. We should also discuss how men can help tackle violence against women and girls.

turns.speaker: Alison Hume
turns.text: We have limited Chamber time. Would you accept Westminster Hall so your debate can be close to 19 November?

turns.speaker: Peter Swallow
turns.text: I know the pressures. I’d prefer the Chamber, but I understand the Committee’s constraints and would accept Westminster Hall if that’s what you choose.

turns.speaker: Chair
turns.text: Would you want the debate on 19 November itself?

turns.speaker: Peter Swallow
turns.text: Ideally yes—preferably first debate of the day on 19 November. If that isn’t possible, a Tuesday in Westminster Hall would also work.

turns.speaker: Chair
turns.text: Noted. The Clerks will be in touch.

chapters.title: Safety of frontier AI: what Iqbal Mohamed asked for
chapters.takeaway: Mr Mohamed urged urgent, high-profile parliamentary scrutiny of advanced AI risks, suggested pharma-style regulation could help, and said he'd accept Westminster Hall if the Chamber wasn't available.

turns.speaker: Chair
turns.text: Next application: Iqbal Mohamed for a Chamber debate on the safety of frontier AI.

turns.speaker: Iqbal Mohamed
turns.text: AI is everywhere. It’s a huge opportunity but also a big risk. I want a Chamber debate so Parliament can act faster than it often does in other areas of policy.

turns.speaker: Iqbal Mohamed
turns.text: The risks are technical, societal and humanitarian. Company leaders have spoken about existential risks—estimates around 10–25%—and Bill Gates has said AI could replace about 40% of jobs.

turns.speaker: Iqbal Mohamed
turns.text: I was the first MP to secure an AI safety debate in Westminster Hall in December 2025; the technology’s pace means we need more attention now to design a regulatory framework that protects people while allowing benefits.

turns.speaker: Iqbal Mohamed
turns.text: From my 25 years in pharmaceuticals, I think principles from pharma regulation—rigorous testing and oversight across the supply chain—could be adapted for AI.

turns.speaker: Jonathan Davies
turns.text: There’s a long waiting list for Chamber time and it can be shortened by urgent statements. Would you accept Westminster Hall if it means getting the debate sooner?

turns.speaker: Iqbal Mohamed
turns.text: Yes—Chamber would give greater public attention, but Westminster Hall is fine if it means the debate happens earlier.

turns.speaker: Jonathan Davies
turns.text: Would you prefer Tuesday or Thursday?

turns.speaker: Iqbal Mohamed
turns.text: Either is fine, though Tuesday is slightly preferable because more MPs are usually present.

turns.speaker: Chair
turns.text: If it’s a Tuesday, which Department would be expected to answer the debate?

turns.speaker: Iqbal Mohamed
turns.text: I believe DCMS now handles digital issues and AI, and there’s an AI Minister attached to the relevant department.

turns.speaker: Martin Vickers
turns.text: Isn’t it Business—whichever name they’re using this week?

turns.speaker: Alison Hume
turns.text: DSIT doesn’t exist now.

turns.speaker: Iqbal Mohamed
turns.text: It’s been reorganised and responsibilities are combined, so you might see cross-departmental coverage.

turns.speaker: Chair
turns.text: Thank you. The Clerks will be back in touch about allocation.

turns.speaker: Iqbal Mohamed
turns.text: Thank you. I appreciate the Committee’s time.
